short_description: Major Shakti Peetha and Tantric center dedicated to Goddess Kamakhya; worship focuses on the yoni rather than an idol. Famous for Ambubachi Mela.
historical_significance: One of 51 ancient Shakti Peethas; core Tantric tradition; 8th–9th century origins with major 16th-century reconstructions; ten Mahavidyas complex.
entry_fee_details: General darshan free; Special darshan approx. ₹50
embedding_text: Kamakhya Temple is a major Shakti Peetha and Tantric center dedicated to Goddess Kamakhya in Guwahati. One of 51 ancient Shakti Peethas with 8th-9th century origins. Known for Ambubachi Mela, Tantric traditions, and Mahavidyas complex.

short_description: 17th-century Shiva shrine on the river island; heritage site and habitat for Golden Langurs. Accessible by ferry from Kachari Ghat or Panbazar Ghat.
historical_significance: Built in 17th century; sacred shrine on river island with rare habitat for endangered Golden Langurs.
food_options: Limited packaged snacks, water available on island
embedding_text: Umananda Temple on Peacock Island is a 17th-century Shiva shrine in the Brahmaputra River. Accessible by ferry, it's home to rare Golden Langurs and offers a unique river island experience with heritage architecture.

address: Range Forest Office, Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary, Raja Mayang, Morigaon District
short_description: High density of one-horned Indian rhinoceros in a compact sanctuary; floodplain grassland ecosystem spanning ~38.8 sq. km. World's highest density of Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros.
historical_significance: Critical rhino conservation site; migratory bird hub; endangered ecosystem.
food_options: Local stalls, canteens near Range Forest Office
nearby_hotels: Rhino and River Wildlife Retreat & Spa
embedding_text: Pobitora Wildlife Sanctuary near Morigaon is home to the world's highest density of one-horned Indian rhinoceros. Located in a floodplain grassland ecosystem, it's a critical conservation site and popular destination for safari and wildlife viewing.

short_description: Historic 18th-century hermitage and temple complex framed by mountain streams; marks the sacred hermitage of sage Vasistha. Serene location with natural water features.
historical_significance: 18th-century hermitage associated with sage Vasistha; mountain stream setting; cultural and spiritual significance.
food_options: Small local food stalls, tea vendors
embedding_text: Basistha Temple is an 18th-century hermitage and temple complex in Guwahati, marked by sacred mountain streams and associated with sage Vasistha. A serene destination near the city center.

address: South-western Guwahati, Kamrup Metropolitan District, Assam 781035
short_description: Wetland of international importance designated as a Ramsar site; major birding hub, marshland habitat, and city stormwater reservoir. Home to vulnerable and rare migratory species.
historical_significance: Ramsar-designated wetland; critical habitat for vulnerable species; city ecology.
entry_fee_details: No entry fees; boat rides under conservation guidelines
embedding_text: Deepor Beel is an internationally designated Ramsar wetland in Guwahati and a major birding destination. Home to vulnerable species like Spot-billed Pelicans and Greater Adjutant Storks, it's a critical habitat for migratory waterfowl.

short_description: Expansive 17.5-hectare cultural complex dedicated to preserving Assamese and Northeast arts, heritage museums, and performing arts. Showcases traditional crafts and regular cultural shows.
historical_significance: Modern cultural institution dedicated to Assamese heritage and Northeast art preservation.
entry_fee_details: Museum galleries: nominal fees; Light/sound shows: additional ticket
embedding_text: Srimanta Sankardev Kalakshetra is a 17.5-hectare cultural complex in Guwahati dedicated to Assamese and Northeast art preservation. Features heritage museums, traditional crafts, open-air amphitheater, and regular cultural performances.
